source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Record the date, time, and location of the safety check.
3. Note the brand, model, and identification number (if available) of the appliance.
4. Identify and document the type of test performed. This may include but not be limited to:
   - PAT (Portable Appliance Testing)
   - Visual Inspection
   - Functional Check
   - Fault Diagnosis
   - Earthing Continuity Check
5. Document the specific failed safety check result details, including:
   - Failed test result: Indicate the failing criteria (e.g., earth resistance, insulation resistance, "trip" time of an RCD)
   - Description of observed faults: Detail any visual defects, abnormal operation, signs of overheating, or damage.
6. Provide detailed notes on any observations or findings that contributed to the failure.
   - For example, frayed cables, incorrect fuses, exposed live parts, etc.
7. Record readings from test instruments
